chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Fadl Abu al-Abbas al-Baqqaq, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is the man more entitled to his child, or the woman?' He said, 'No, rather the man. And if the woman says to her husband who divorced her, "I will breastfeed my son like the one who breastfeeds him," she is more entitled to him.'
ai.seo_question: Who has more right to custody of a child after divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the hierarchy of custody rights, establishing that while the father holds primary entitlement, the mother’s right to breastfeed (radāʿ) serves as a decisive exception that grants her priority. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the practical capability and right to nurture the child through breastfeeding can supersede the father's general claim, reflecting a nuanced balance between paternal authority and maternal care. The hadith highlights the importance of the nursing period as a legal determinant in family law, ensuring the child's welfare remains central to custody decisions.
